title: Duo Push Fraud Detection
exclusions: Covers Duo Push only. Phone-call and SMS fatigue use different factors; extend the `factor` list if those are allowed in your policies.
evidence: Saved alert results with the push counts, source IPs, and countries, plus the incident record showing the password reset and session revocation for confirmed cases.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Sign in to a Duo-protected test application as a test user five times in a few minutes, deny three of the pushes, and mark one as fraud. The search returns one row for the user with `fraud` at least 1 and `denied` at least 3.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Sign in once as the same user and approve the push. The event is indexed, but the search returns no row.

dataSources: `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input, Authentication log type, which polls `GET /admin/v2/logs/authentication`. One JSON event per authentication or enrollment attempt with `event_type`, `result`, `reason`, `factor`, `user.name`, `application.name`, `access_device.*`, and `auth_device.*`.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Cisco Duo input. Replaces the deprecated Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026).
spl:
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:authentication_v2" event_type="authentication" factor IN ("duo_push", "verified_duo_push")
| eval result=lower(result), user=coalesce('user.name', username), src='access_device.ip', country='access_device.location.country', app_name='application.name'
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count as pushes sum(eval(if(result="denied", 1, 0))) as denied sum(eval(if(result="fraud", 1, 0))) as fraud sum(eval(if(result="success", 1, 0))) as approved values(src) as src values(country) as countries values(app_name) as applications by _time user
| where fraud > 0 OR (pushes >= 5 AND denied >= 3)
| eval severity=case(approved > 0, "critical", fraud > 0, "high", true(), "medium")
| sort - severity, - pushes
description: Finds Duo Push sessions where the user reported the push as fraud (`result=fraud`, reason `user_marked_fraud`) or where five or more pushes with three or more denials hit one user in ten minutes. Severity is critical when any push in the burst was approved.
value: Push bombing is how attackers with a stolen password get past MFA: they send pushes until a tired user approves one. A fraud report or a denial burst means the password is already compromised. If one push was approved, the attacker is probably signed in now.
implementation: Collect the Duo Authentication log (v2) with the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input into `index=duo`. Schedule every 5 minutes over the last 10 minutes. Treat critical rows as an incident: revoke sessions and reset the password.
visualization: Alert table: _time, user, severity, pushes, denied, fraud, approved, src, countries, applications. Supporting panel: daily count of fraud reports and push bursts over 90 days (column chart).

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Accidental fraud reports** — users sometimes tap "Report" instead of "Deny". Confirm with the user, but treat it as real until confirmed.

2. **Retry loops** — a client application that retries a failed sign-in sends several pushes in a row. These come from one source IP that is the user's usual address, and usually have no approvals.

**Suppression:** none for fraud reports. Throttle denial bursts per user for 1 hour.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs. It replaces the Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026); disable the old connector's inputs after cutover so events are not indexed twice.
• A Duo Admin API application created by an Owner-role administrator in the Duo Admin Panel under Applications > Protect an Application > Admin API. Record the integration key, secret key, and API hostname (`api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com`), and grant it **Grant read log**.
• Outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from the input host to the API hostname, and an accurate system clock on that host, because the Admin API signs every request with the current date.
• An index for Duo data (this page uses `index=duo`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the identity and SOC teams.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Cisco Duo card, and create an input with the integration key, secret key, and API hostname. Enable the Authentication log type (the v2 endpoint, not Authentication Legacy v1) and set the index to `duo`.
• The input reads `GET /admin/v2/logs/authentication` and writes `sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2`. `result` is one of `success`, `denied`, `failure`, `error`, or `fraud` in lowercase; the legacy v1 type `cisco:duo:authentication` uses uppercase values, so the searches lowercase `result` before comparing.
• Device-posture fields under `access_device` (`is_encryption_enabled`, `is_firewall_enabled`, `is_password_set`, `security_agents`) are filled only when the application uses the Duo Universal Prompt and Duo Desktop is installed, and only on Duo Premier or Advantage plans.
• Check the fields this search needs: run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2 | stats count by factor result` over 7 days and confirm `duo_push` and the lowercase results appear.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:authentication_v2" event_type="authentication" factor IN ("duo_push", "verified_duo_push")
| eval result=lower(result), user=coalesce('user.name', username), src='access_device.ip', country='access_device.location.country', app_name='application.name'
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count as pushes sum(eval(if(result="denied", 1, 0))) as denied sum(eval(if(result="fraud", 1, 0))) as fraud sum(eval(if(result="success", 1, 0))) as approved values(src) as src values(country) as countries values(app_name) as applications by _time user
| where fraud > 0 OR (pushes >= 5 AND denied >= 3)
| eval severity=case(approved > 0, "critical", fraud > 0, "high", true(), "medium")
| sort - severity, - pushes
```

Understanding this SPL
• The first line limits the search to Duo Push and Verified Duo Push attempts.
• `result=fraud` is set only when the user taps Report on the push; Duo then records the reason `user_marked_fraud`.
• `stats` in 10-minute bins counts pushes, denials, fraud reports, and approvals per user, so one row describes one burst.
• `severity` is critical when any push was approved, because the attacker likely got in; high for a fraud report alone; medium for a denial burst.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Duo admin console (Admin Panel) under Reports > Authentication Log for the same user and time range: each attempt listed there should appear in `index=duo` with the same result and reason.
• For a fraud row, confirm the attempt shows as Fraud in the Admin Panel and that the user received a fraud notification if your account sends them.
• Run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:authentication_v2 | timechart span=1h count by result` over 7 days; gaps longer than two input intervals point to collection failures, not quiet periods.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule every 5 minutes over the last 10 minutes and throttle on `user` for 1 hour.
• Page the SOC on critical and high rows. Response: revoke the user's sessions in the identity provider, reset the password, and check the user's sign-ins from `src` after the approved push.
• Send to Enterprise Security as a finding with the user as the risk object when ES is in use.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No Duo events and HTTP 401 in the input log under `$SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/duo_splunkapp/`: wrong secret key, an API hostname from a different Duo account, or clock skew on the input host.
• HTTP 403: the Admin API application is missing **Grant read log**.
• HTTP 429: Duo rate-limits the log endpoints. Make sure the deprecated 3504 connector and the 7404 input are not both polling the same Admin API application.
• Duplicate rows after migration: the 3504 connector and the 7404 input are both enabled for the same log type.
• Searches return nothing but events exist: the input is on Authentication Legacy v1, so events are in `cisco:duo:authentication` with uppercase `result` and flat `username`. Switch the input to the v2 log type rather than editing the searches.
• Missing fields `user.name` or `access_device.ip`: the events were indexed before `KV_MODE=json` applied, or a custom props stanza overrides the add-on. Check `| fieldsummary` on one hour of data.
• Fraud reports in the Admin Panel but no rows: your account uses `factor` values with different casing (for example `Duo Push`) from the v1 log. Check `| stats count by factor` and add the value.
grandmaExplanation: We alert when someone gets flooded with login approval requests on their phone or reports one as fake, because that means a stranger has their password.
